subthemes.name: Predicting what comes next
subthemes.gist: The core problem: given past values in a sequence, predict future ones. Papers explore neural networks, decomposition, frequency analysis, and hybrid approaches to make better forecasts.

subthemes.name: Generating sequences with diffusion and flows
subthemes.gist: Using modern generative models—diffusion, flow matching, and neural ODEs—to synthesize realistic time series data or transform sequences for imputation and forecasting.

subthemes.name: Finding the unusual and the break
subthemes.gist: Spotting when a time series behaves abnormally or suddenly changes character. This includes detecting anomalies, change points, and out-of-distribution events in sequences.

subthemes.name: Pairing sequences with language
subthemes.gist: Bridging time series and text by learning from paired descriptions, using language models to reason about sequences, or generating narratives from temporal data.

subthemes.name: Learning patterns that transfer
subthemes.gist: Building foundation models and using transfer learning so that knowledge learned on one time series task or dataset generalizes to new ones without retraining from scratch.

subthemes.name: Working with very few parameters
subthemes.gist: Lightweight models that run fast and need little memory—from linear regressions to pruned networks—for when data is scarce or compute is tight.

subthemes.name: Understanding why the model predicts
subthemes.gist: Making time series models interpretable and explainable—showing which past values matter, why anomalies occur, or what causal patterns the model has found.

subthemes.name: Handling messy real-world sequences
subthemes.gist: Time series in the wild have missing values, irregular sampling, mixed data types, and corruptions. Papers tackle imputation, asynchrony, multimodality, and robustness to these challenges.

subthemes.name: Adapting models across domains
subthemes.gist: Time series models trained on one source (e.g., one hospital or factory) often fail elsewhere. Papers tackle domain adaptation, generalization, and alignment to new environments.
